title: A damaged plant's health bar eats clicks on the playfield
description: Plant._health_back and _health_bar are ColorRects with the default MOUSE_FILTER_STOP, parked over the playfield. A damaged plant therefore has a 32x5 strip that swallows clicks meant for the board. Pre-existing; found while adding the health bar notches.

title: Post-mortem calls your best chokepoint your weakest ground
description: Game._note_lane_loss is called from _on_pest_died (every kill, at the pest's position) as well as _on_pest_escaped. So _run_losses counts kills, not damage. That is correct for LanePressureOverlay, whose doc says 'how far did pests get' - a kill at cell 30 of 40 IS pressure. But run_summary.gd:201 _worst_cell_text() labels the highest-count cell 'Weakest ground - N lost there', so a well-defended chokepoint is reported to the player as their weakest ground, every run. The advice is not just useless, it is inverted. Found by the agent building the prep depth readout, which declined to reuse worst_run_cell() for exactly this reason.

title: A truncated save silently zeroes a high score that can never be restored
description: RunConfig._save stamps a SAVE_VERSION line on every write and _load tests only begins_with('v') -- the version is written and never actually read, so a future format change has no migration hook despite the field existing to provide one. Worse, int('') is 0 in GDScript, so a truncated or partially-written save loads as a zero high score, and record_score only ever raises a record: once it reads 0 the real number is gone forever with no way back. A save file is the one thing in this project the player cannot regenerate by playing.
acceptance_criteria: A malformed, truncated or short save leaves the existing in-memory scores untouched rather than zeroing them, and the version field is actually consulted. Unit tests cover a truncated file, a garbage file, and a future version number.

title: Quitting an endless run through pause files no score
description: RunConfig.record_score has exactly one caller, Game._end_run, reached only from the victory branch or from lives hitting 0. has_more_waves() is unconditionally true in endless, so victory is unreachable there -- meaning the ONLY way to bank an endless score is to lose. Cycle 8's pause screen then added two exits that bypass _end_run entirely: RestartButton calls reload_current_scene and GateButton calls change_scene_to_file. So a player who quits a long endless run voluntarily files nothing, and the run they were most likely to be proud of is the one guaranteed not to count.
acceptance_criteria: Leaving a run through any exit files the score exactly once, and a re-entry cannot file it twice. Unit test covers quitting via both pause exits.

title: Uproot-as-score: refunds credit seeds_earned_total, so plant-uproot cycling inflates the high score
description: SeedBank.refund routes through add_seeds, which increments seeds_earned_total -- the number both per-mode high scores are kept on. So planting a Corn for 10 and uprooting it for 6 costs 4 seeds of wallet and CREDITS 6 to the recorded score, repeatably. A 100-seed float converts to roughly +150 score with no gameplay at all. Scaling the refund by health in cycle 7 killed uproot-as-repair and left this untouched; the seed_bank comment 'Refunds count too' documents the behaviour as deliberate, but it predates high scores being a scoreboard players compete on.
acceptance_criteria: Uprooting cannot raise seeds_earned_total. A unit test plants and uproots in a loop and asserts the recorded score does not move, while ordinary income still counts.

title: Common seed packets silently become rare ones once Chomp unlocks
description: SeedBank._roll_packet filters the locked pool to ids at or below the packet's max_tier, then falls back to the WHOLE locked pool when that filtered pool is empty. Chomp is tier 1 and Sunflower is tier 2, so the moment Chomp unlocks the filtered pool for a common packet is always empty and a 20-seed common packet can hand out the tier-2 Sunflower. That makes the two packet tiers indistinguishable in the only way they were supposed to differ, and both tooltips become false: the common button says 'tier 1 only' and the rare one says 'the only reliable way to a Seed Sunflower'.
acceptance_criteria: A common packet can never yield a plant above its max_tier. When nothing at or below that tier remains locked, the purchase is refused with a reason rather than silently upgraded, and the tooltips match the behaviour. Unit test covers the exhausted-pool case.
close_reason: Common packets refuse rather than falling back to the whole locked pool; no charge on refusal, no soft-lock possible. Fixed a pre-existing test that was green only because of the bug.

title: Style contract + first sprite set (Corn Cobbler, Chomp Flower, pests, seed packet)
description: Measured the Kenney Tower Defense kit's conventions into art_src/STYLE.md, authored 6 SVG sources, rasterised them to assets/sprites (64) + retina (128), and gated the contract with test/unit/test_sprite_style.gd.

title: A budgets verb that prints every declared coupling with its headroom
description: Four constants now carry 'moving me costs you X' comments: PATH_CORNERS, COLLECT_RADIUS, SUBHEAD_MAX_WIDTH and the HUD WORST_CASE_TEXT budgets. Each warns about a coupling living in another file, and a person only finds the warning by editing that exact line. A devtools verb printing every declared budget with its current headroom makes the set visible before someone goes looking.

title: Name the husk budget where the road is actually edited
description: board_info now reports the husk click budget, but reaching it needs a running game, a launched bridge and knowing the verb exists. A designer dragging Board.PATH_CORNERS is in board.gd in an editor and nothing there mentions the budget. Add a ## line above PATH_CORNERS and above CompostMeter.COLLECT_RADIUS naming it. Suggested by the agent that built the devtools half, which correctly judged its own work a half-solution.

title: Give the board a second warning channel so red is not carrying three meanings
description: GardenTheme.DANGER now paints lane pressure (pests got this far), the plant health bar (this plant is dying) and an armed Uproot (you are about to destroy this). Three different sentences in one hue at three alphas. Unifying the value was right; colour alone should not carry three meanings - add a shape or hatch channel.

title: Put husk_click_margin in board_info so the budget is visible before a test fails
description: husk_click_margin() exists because the husk-vs-placement conflict is 4px from being real, and a test asserts the clearance stays positive. Nothing tells a designer moving PATH_CORNERS or COLLECT_RADIUS that they are spending it - they find out when a test fails, with no indication 4px was the budget.

title: Show lane pressure during prep, not after the run
description: LanePressureOverlay paints how far pests got, decayed once per wave, and is a readout of the wave that just ended. Board.run_pressure_alpha exists and is shown exactly once by show_run_pressure(), at the moment the run is over. The number that would inform a purchase is held back until purchasing has stopped. Surface it during the prep strip.

title: The notebook is unreachable the moment a run starts
description: NotebookScreen is constructed in exactly one place, title_screen.gd's _open_notebook(), and nothing in game.gd, hud.gd or pause_screen.gd can reach it. So the game's only explanation of anything is closed to the player who actually needs it -- mid-run, holding a plant they do not understand. The pause card is now a full-screen surface that already lists the keyboard verbs and is already the only way to leave a run; a fourth button on it is the whole fix. NotebookScreen already emits back_requested and is built to be added as a child of any Control.
acceptance_criteria: The notebook opens from within a run and returns to the paused game, with the run still paused behind it. A test asserts the pause state survives opening and closing it.

title: The endless spawn gap floors at wave 22 and only the count keeps climbing
description: WaveDirector's aphid spawn gap reaches its floor around wave 22, and the health and speed scales cap around waves 41 and 48. Past 48 the only thing that still moves is count, which is uncapped -- 166 pests at wave 48, 376 at wave 108. Spawn floor times crossing time puts on the order of 100 aphids alive at once on an 896px board. That is precisely the quantity problem the ENDLESS_HEALTH_STEP header says the scales exist to avoid, arrived at from the other direction.
acceptance_criteria: Endless difficulty past the scale caps escalates by something other than raw count, or count is bounded and the difficulty comes from elsewhere. A test asserts simultaneous pest count stays under a stated ceiling at wave 100.

title: A husk eats the click that would have planted, and the preview cannot warn about it
description: CompostMeter.COLLECT_RADIUS is 28, so a husk claims a 56px-wide target on a 64px cell -- 88% of it. Game._click_at sweeps a husk before it reaches the placement branch and returns, so a click on a cell the preview has just drawn as legal composts instead of planting. PlacementPreview now computes four states (illegal, at_risk, dead ground, redundant coverage) and mentions husks exactly zero times, so the one thing that can silently take the click is the one thing the ring cannot warn about. Husks last up to 10s, so the cell is effectively unplantable for that long with no indication.
acceptance_criteria: Either the preview shows that a click on this cell will compost rather than plant, or placement wins on a cell the player has explicitly targeted. Unit test covers a husk overlapping a buildable cell.
close_reason: Precedence fixed: a click that would plant, plants. Measurement showed the conflict cannot occur on the shipping board (32px vs a 28px sweep, 4px margin) -- husk_click_margin() now gates that

title: Every Sundew redraw walks every pest on the board
description: StickySundew._draw_wash calls shared_ground_offsets, which calls _sibling_patches, which walks all of _entities' children -- and pests live there too. So the cost of drawing one patch scales with the number of pests, not the number of patches. _refresh_droplets queues a redraw whenever droplet_radius changes, which it does as pests enter and leave the patch, so the redraws are most frequent exactly when the pest count is highest. Sundew membership changes at only two sites, so the sibling list could be cached and invalidated there instead.
acceptance_criteria: Drawing a patch does not iterate pests. A test asserts the sibling lookup is not called per-pest, or that redraw cost is independent of pest count.

title: The 45-seed Corn upgrade is worse than the 20-seed one against a single pest
description: CornCobbler.LEVELS with evenly-spaced offsets puts level 3's kernels at +/-26, +/-13 and 0 degrees. Against Kernel.HIT_RADIUS 18.0 an outer kernel clears the aimed pest past 18/tan(26) = 37px -- under one cell, against a RANGE of 176. Level 2's +/-7 degrees connects out to 147px. Single-target that is level 2 at 2.78 dps versus level 3 at 1.61, and damage is 1.0 at all three levels. So the most expensive upgrade in the game makes a cob worse against the thing it is aimed at, while the selection panel advertises '5 kernel(s) per shot' and the muzzle fan draws the spread as the benefit.
acceptance_criteria: Each upgrade level is at least as good as the one below it against a single target, or the spread's cost is stated where the player buys it. A test asserts single-target dps is non-decreasing across levels.

title: The pause note is drawn underneath the first button
description: PauseScreen.FIRST_BUTTON_Y is an absolute 232.0 -- the one offset in that file not written as CARD.position.y + N. With CARD at y=152 the Note's box is 228-252 and ResumeButton's is 232-276, so 20 of the note's 24 pixels sit under an opaque stylebox. There is 64px of unused card below the last button. This is a sibling-pair overlap, the class validate-ui and findings structurally cannot see because each Control fits its own box; the repo ships .claude/skills/godot-hud-occlusion-audit for exactly this. The note text is also a constant, 'The wave is waiting.', which is false whenever pause fires between waves.
acceptance_criteria: No pause-screen Control overlaps another, asserted by a pairwise test, and the note says something true about the current state.

title: Two Sundews on the same ground cost 60 seeds and slow nothing extra
description: StickySundew refcounts its slow so overlapping patches hold a pest at 0.55 rather than 0.30 -- correct, and deliberate. But the patch wash composites darker where two patches overlap, so the only thing on screen says the opposite of the rule: it reads as 'more slow here'. A player can spend 60 seeds on two patches covering the same road and get exactly what one would have given. The placement preview has no notion of ground already covered, and crossing_time_multiplier() has no caller outside a test.
acceptance_criteria: Overlapping Sundew ground is visually distinguishable from stacked-and-working, or the preview warns before the second one is placed. A test covers the overlap case.

title: There is no pause, and no way to leave a run you are done with
description: get_tree().paused appears nowhere in game/. Game._unhandled_input handles motion, left click, KEY_R gated on game over, and KEY_M for mute -- there is no pause key. PREP_SECONDS keeps counting down while the player is away from the keyboard, so stepping away mid-run loses beds. TITLE_SCENE is reachable only from RunSummary's GateButton, which means the only way out of a run in progress is to lose it or kill the process. The devtools bridge answers while the tree is paused, so a pause menu is verifiable.
acceptance_criteria: A pause key freezes the run including the prep timer, and offers a way back to the title screen. Unit test asserts the prep timer does not advance while paused.

title: Nothing in the catalogue answers a hungry pest
description: Sticky Sundew deliberately does not answer is_hungry: a hungry pest stops to eat a plant at EAT_DPS 14.0 against Plant.MAX_HEALTH 40.0, under three seconds per bed, and eating is not movement-gated so a slow does nothing about it. Every plant in the catalogue either damages a pest or funds the ones that do; nothing protects or repairs a bed under attack. A real answer needs a regen or armour hook on Plant, which is why it was filed rather than faked.
acceptance_criteria: A plant, upgrade or mechanic exists that meaningfully changes the outcome when a hungry pest reaches a bed. Unit test drives a hungry pest against a defended and an undefended bed and asserts the difference.

title: A plant's health only goes down, and the cheapest repair is to destroy it
description: Plant.take_damage is the only writer of health and there is no heal path anywhere. uproot_refund reads PlantCatalog.cost * 0.6 and never reads health, so uprooting a nearly-dead plant refunds exactly as much as uprooting a pristine one -- making uproot-and-replant the cheapest repair in the game at a net 4 seeds for a Corn. That is a strictly dominant strategy that also makes the new health readout advisory rather than a decision.
acceptance_criteria: Either damaged plants can be healed at a cost, or the uproot refund scales with remaining health so a wrecked plant refunds less. Unit test covers the refund at full and near-zero health.

title: The placement ring is drawn with equal confidence over cells that cover no road at all
description: PlacementPreview computes reach and legality per cell but legality only means buildable-and-empty. Measured against the real PATH_CORNERS route: of 94 buildable cells, 15 cover zero road at a Corn Cobbler's RANGE of 176px, and 34 cover zero road at a Chomp Flower's GRAB_RADIUS of 73.6px. The ring looks identical on all of them, so a player can spend 10 seeds on a plant that can never fire, and nothing says so before or after the click.
acceptance_criteria: A cell that covers no road for the currently selected plant is visually distinct in the preview before the click. Unit test asserts the covered-road count per cell against the real route for both plants.

title: One high score serves both game modes, and the title screen names it wrong
description: Game._end_run calls RunConfig.record_score with the run's seed total and no mode check, and RunConfig persists a single number to user://highscore.save. TitleScreen renders that one number as 'Best endless run' / 'No endless run on record yet'. So a campaign run can take the endless record, and RunSummary._score_line then compares a campaign total against a number that may have come from an endless run. Two different games are sharing one scoreboard and the label claims otherwise.
acceptance_criteria: Campaign and endless keep separate high scores, each labelled for the mode it came from, and an existing single-value save migrates without being lost. Unit test covers a campaign run not overwriting an endless record.

title: The game makes no sound at all
description: A repo-wide grep for AudioStreamPlayer, AudioStream, .ogg and .wav finds no hit anywhere in game code -- assets/ holds only kenney/ and sprites/. Four new cues shipped in cycle 3-4 (uproot arming, plant damage, threat escalation, mutation markers) and not one of them makes a noise. The silent-death case is the worst: compost_meter erases an expired husk with no cue at all, so the player never learns they were too slow. Kenney ships CC0 audio packs in the same collection the sprites came from.
acceptance_criteria: At least placement, pest death, husk collection, husk rot and run end have distinct sounds, with a master mute honoured (devtools_config.json already sets mute:true for automation). A test asserts every declared sound file exists and loads.
close_reason: 11 CC0 Kenney samples, 8-voice root-parented pool, silent-husk-rot fixed; verified live catching a voice mid-playback and surviving a scene reload

title: A mutated pest is a tint, and the two that change the rules are unnamed
description: Pest mutations are signalled only by a _tint colour. Winged makes a Chomp Flower unable to grab it at all (chomp_flower.gd skips pests with is_winged) and hungry makes it eat a plant at EAT_DPS 14.0 against Plant.MAX_HEALTH 40.0 -- under three seconds to destroy a bed. Both change what the player should do and neither is named or shaped differently. The placement preview already computes at_risk, so the vocabulary for warning about this exists.
acceptance_criteria: A winged and a hungry pest are each distinguishable from a plain one by something other than hue -- a shape, an icon, or a label -- and the distinction survives a screenshot in greyscale.

title: Nothing counts down the 18 seconds to the next wave
description: Game.PREP_SECONDS is 18.0 and _process silently decrements _prep_left until a wave starts on its own. The only mention is a 6-second message when the previous wave clears, so for the other 12 seconds the player has no idea how long they have to spend seeds and place plants. The threat tint now tells them how bad the next wave is and still nothing tells them when it lands.
acceptance_criteria: The HUD shows the remaining prep time and it visibly counts down; the readout disappears once a wave is live. Covered by a unit test that pumps _process and asserts the text changes.

title: The message line has one slot, so cues stomp each other
description: Hud.show_message assigns _message_label.text outright and resets a single _message_left timer, so any new message destroys the one before it mid-read. The uproot gate made this concrete: the 4s 'click again to uproot' instruction is wiped by the 2s husk message the moment a pest dies, and the player is left with an armed button and no explanation. A short queue, or a second line, or at minimum refusing to overwrite a higher-priority message before it has been readable.
acceptance_criteria: A message cannot be replaced before a minimum readable time unless the new one is higher priority; the uproot instruction survives an incidental husk pickup. Unit test drives two overlapping show_message calls and asserts what the label reads.

title: A real end-of-run summary panel
description: _end_run paints the run's whole damage map on the board and names the worst cell in a 30s message that expires while the player is still reading the banner. Every number a post-mortem needs is already computed -- waves survived, threat level reached, seeds earned, high score, worst lane cell, husks collected vs dropped. Give them a panel that stays until dismissed, instead of a banner plus a timed message.
acceptance_criteria: An end-of-run panel showing at least waves survived, threat level reached, seeds earned and the worst lane cell, which persists until the player restarts; covered by a headless UI test.
close_reason: RunSummary card with waves/threat/beds/compost/worst-cell, persists until dismissed, replay and back-to-title both wired and verified live

title: Show a selected plant's health in the side panel
description: Hungry pests chew plants down over several seconds and Plant.health drives a bar on the plant itself, but the selection panel shows only the name and blurb. Selecting a half-eaten Corn Cobbler tells the player nothing about whether to uproot and replant it, which is exactly the decision the panel exists to support. Add a health readout to the selection box.
acceptance_criteria: The selection panel shows current/max health for a damaged plant and updates as it takes damage; a unit test drives take_damage and asserts the panel text changed.
close_reason: Health bar + numbers in the selection panel, hidden until damaged, green->red ramp; runtime caught a zero-margin panel foot which is now fixed and gated at 8px

title: Uproot needs a confirm or an undo
description: The Uproot button refunds 60% and destroys the plant instantly with no confirmation. One stray click on a selected Sunflower late in a run silently destroys the economy the whole run was built on -- it is the only irreversible misclick in the game. Add a confirm step (the button re-labels to 'Uproot? Confirm' for a few seconds) or a short undo window that restores the plant and reverses the refund.
acceptance_criteria: A single click on Uproot does not remove the plant; a second within the window does. Unit tests cover both the confirm path and the timeout-cancels path.
close_reason: request_uproot() arms on first click, commits on a second within 4s; verified live (232x40 relabel, exact UPROOT_ARMED red, timeout revert) and covered by 4 tests

title: Designer's Notebook reads as two floating images, not a notebook
description: Six pages, each a bare 320x320 drawing beside a bare 320x320 sprite on a flat dark field, with one six-word green caption and three default buttons below. Nothing says which pane is which, the sprite renders blurry (64px source filtered up to 320), there is no keyboard paging or Escape, no transition between pages, and the page/sprite mapping is wrong in places (image6 is the named Corn Cobbler portrait, not the kernel volley; image3 is where the kernels are).
acceptance_criteria: A paper spread with a binding so it reads as a notebook; per-pane headings; crisp sprite rendering; a real designer note per page, not just a caption; correct drawing-to-sprite mapping; page dots; Left/Right arrows page and Escape closes; a cross-fade between pages; Drawing/Sprite/PageLabel/Backdrop stay direct children of the root so existing tests and bridge paths hold.

title: Title screen is a flat rectangle with default-theme buttons
description: The title screen draws INK over the whole viewport, three stock grey Buttons and three Labels. No art, no motion, no keyboard, and the bottom third is empty — in a game that already ships plant and pest sprites. It is the first thing a player sees and it looks unfinished.
acceptance_criteria: A themed button set (paper/ink/leaf, hover + focus states); a drawn backdrop instead of one flat colour; the game's own sprites on screen; an entrance animation that is skipped headlessly; keyboard focus and Enter to start; existing node paths (Backdrop/StartButton/EndlessButton/NotebookButton) unchanged so tests and the bridge still resolve.

title: HUD compost counter collides with the Grow-the-next-wave button
description: With several husks on the ground the HUD reads 'Compost 0 (11 ready)' and the '(11 ready)' suffix runs underneath the 'Grow the next wave' button. Caught in a screenshot during /verify on 2026-08-15; validate-ui reported 0 findings over that exact frame because the label's own rect is fine -- it is the button that overlaps it, and nothing compares two sibling Controls for occlusion. Give the HUD bar a real layout (HBoxContainer with the button in its own slot) so the counter cannot be run over regardless of how long its text gets.
acceptance_criteria: A HUD with a 2-digit husk count and the wave button both visible has no overlapping screen rects, asserted by node-bounds in a test.

title: Mutated pests should drop a better husk
description: Armoured/winged/hungry mutations all cost the player more to deal with than a plain pest, but _on_pest_died pays the same husk value regardless of mutation. Scale husk value by mutation (e.g. armoured/winged/hungry each worth more) to tie the mutation system into the compost system instead of leaving them side by side.
close_reason: Pest.husk_multiplier() scales husk value by mutation (armoured/winged 1.5x, hungry 2x); verified headless (4 unit tests) and live (compost_state: plain=2, hungry=3)

title: Lane pressure readout on the road
description: The board is a single road, so which end pests got furthest on last wave is always answerable but never shown. Tint the road segment red where pests advanced furthest last wave, fading each wave, to give the player a passive read on lane pressure without opening any menu.
close_reason: LanePressureOverlay tints the road cell where pests got furthest last wave; verified headless (4 unit tests, one of which caught a real game-over-mid-wave commit bug) and live (board_info + run-method + screenshot)

title: Selection needs a second cue beyond the range ring
description: Right now the only sign a plant is selected is the translucent range ring — Corn Cobbler shows it, but Chomp Flower draws no ring at all, so selecting a Chomp shows nothing. Add a thin outline or corner brackets drawn on the sprite itself in the base Plant class (not per-subclass), so selection is legible for every current and future plant.
close_reason: SelectionMarker child node ships in Plant, verified headless (2 unit tests) and at runtime (get-state + screenshot)

title: Corn range indicator on selected plant
description: Placement is blind: corn reaches 176px and nothing shows it. Draw a range ring around the plant when selected/placing so the player can judge coverage.
close_reason: Wired Plant.set_selected() into Game._select() (closes G-007) and added ChompFlower's shrinking chew ring; both verified at runtime via /verify.

title: Chomp Flower occupied readout
description: chew_progress() exists on ChompFlower and nothing draws it. The Chomp/beetle trade-off (mouth busy ~2.6s, lane open) is invisible to the player. Draw a shrinking ring/bar around the flower while chewing.
close_reason: Wired Plant.set_selected() into Game._select() (closes G-007) and added ChompFlower's shrinking chew ring; both verified at runtime via /verify.

title: Sprite pass 2: damaged/eating/dead states
description: The design doc draws a Chomp mid-bite and an X-eyed pest; those are separate sprites, not tints.
close_reason: Implemented and /verify'd in the 2026-08-15 session: sprite pass 2 (eating/dead states), pest mutations from wave 8, tiered seed packets + Seed Sunflower (3rd plant), title screen + endless mode, and the Designer's Notebook screen. See log-devtools.md and kanban.md.

title: Pest waves: aphid swarms and beetle heavies
description: Aphid = fast/weak, Beetle = slow/tanky and survives a Chomp long enough to matter.

title: Chomp Flower melee: instant on small pests, slow chew on big ones
description: 'eats small pests easily, takes a while eating bigger pests' — occupied-while-chewing is the whole balance lever.

title: Corn Cobbler firing: single kernel, then the 'bunch of corn' burst
description: Design doc shows a single projectile upgrading to a spread of kernels.

title: Seed economy: earn seeds, buy seed packets to unlock plants
description: 'You have to buy plant seeds to get plants' — seed drops from killed pests, a packet shop, and a run-persistent unlock set.

title: Plant placement and the one free starter plant
description: Corn Cobbler is free at wave 1 per the design doc; every other plant costs seeds.

title: Grid + path playfield from the Kenney tilesheet
description: Build the top-down lane using assets/kenney/png terrain tiles: dirt path over grass, buildable plots, spawn and base tiles.

title: BLOCKED_COLOR is a hand-typed near-red the palette merge missed
description: PlacementPreview.BLOCKED_COLOR is Color(0.95, 0.42, 0.36, 0.75), a hand-typed near-red that the GardenTheme palette merge did not catch. It should probably alias GardenTheme.DANGER. Note it draws brackets (already a shape channel) rather than a surface, so it is a value change belonging to the merge, not a legibility fix.

title: Separate what is true of a road from what is true of THIS road
description: PATH_CORNERS produces 32 road cells and 2112px of walking. At least four things are calibrated against that route: the endless road budget's pests-per-cell, the Sundew's coverage arithmetic, the dead-ground count of 15 of 94, and the husk clearance. Each is tested individually; a second route would move all four at once and nothing says which are properties of a road and which of this one.

title: The title screen's lawn and the notebook both predate half the catalogue
description: TitleScreen.PLANTS is a literal list of a Sunflower, two Corn Cobblers and a Chomp, chosen when those were the whole catalogue -- the Sticky Sundew is absent, so the first thing a new player sees advertises three quarters of the game. Separately, the notebook's five pages cover the Corn, the packet, the kernel and the Chomp twice; a grep for sunflower or sundew across notebook_screen.gd returns zero, so both tier-2 plants -- the ones unlocked late and least understood -- appear nowhere in the only place the game explains anything.
acceptance_criteria: The lawn is derived from PlantCatalog rather than a literal list, so a new plant appears without anyone remembering, and every plant in the catalogue has a notebook page. A test asserts both against PlantCatalog.ids().

title: Compost swept is a numerator with no denominator
description: CompostMeter gained a husk_rotted signal in the sound pass and Game._on_husk_rotted receives it, plays a sound and increments nothing. So the post-mortem reports 'Compost swept 12' with no way to know whether four rotted or forty did. Every other row on that card is a total or a bound; this is the one that is neither, and the missing half is the one that tells a player whether sweeping is a skill they have.
acceptance_criteria: The post-mortem reports husks missed alongside husks swept, and the counter survives to the end of the run. A unit test drives a husk to rot through the real timer and asserts the count.

title: Two palettes, one game, and the HUD's private half is now the bigger one
description: garden_theme.gd states outright that it does not touch the in-game HUD, and hud.gd re-declares INK, PAPER, PAPER_DARK and LEAF with identical values. That was a fair split when the HUD had four colours. It has since grown UPROOT_ARMED, THREAT_WARM, THREAT_HOT, HEALTH_BACK, HEALTH_FULL and HEALTH_LOW -- six more the title screen, the notebook and the post-mortem cannot reach, even though the post-mortem is a paper card that would want the same red for 'this cost you something'. The HUD references GardenTheme only for animations_enabled().
acceptance_criteria: One palette, reachable from every screen, with the HUD's semantic colours named where the other screens can use them. No colour value is declared twice.

title: Node metadata is a cross-script contract that no gate can see
description: A Sundew's entire slow correctness lives in set_meta on a Pest -- the base speed and the source count are stored under string keys read by another script. title_screen.gd does the same with bare 'speed' and 'offset' literals. Because the keys are strings, name_check.py cannot resolve them, lint and import_check only type-check declarations, and coverage_check.py's eight defect classes are all Controls, signals, orphans, input, scenes, shaders and names. A typo in a metadata key is silent everywhere and produces a plant that simply does nothing.
acceptance_criteria: Something fails when a set_meta key is written in one script and read with a different spelling in another. A parallel-safe checker in name_check.py's shape would fit the existing toolchain.
close_reason: tools/meta_key_check.py gates both ends of every metadata key; corrected the premise -- all five keys are single-file, not cross-script, and the checker labels the difference

title: Four keyboard verbs in a run and no screen names any of them
description: R restarts on game over, Escape and P pause, M mutes. The only mention anywhere is 'Press M to bring it back', printed after you have already found M. The title screen documents its own three keys in a HintLabel, so the convention exists; the run does not follow it. The pause card is the natural home -- it is already a full-screen surface with room, and it is where a player goes when they want to know what their options are.
acceptance_criteria: Every key binding available during a run is discoverable from within the run without pressing it first. A test asserts the listed keys match the ones _unhandled_input actually handles.

title: Two sprite gates and neither can tell you the PNG came from the SVG
description: tools/svg_style_check.py never opens a raster; test/unit/test_sprite_style.gd reads PNGs against a hand-written 12-name EXPECTED_SIZE and never opens a source. So a stale render passes both -- edit an SVG, forget to run render_svg.gd, and every gate stays green over a PNG that no longer matches its source. A 13th SVG is also invisible to the raster gate until someone remembers to add its name.
acceptance_criteria: Something fails when a PNG is older than its SVG, or when an SVG has no corresponding rendered pair. Ideally EXPECTED_SIZE is derived from art_src/ rather than hand-maintained.

title: The rare packet's tooltip names one plant and the packet now holds two
description: Hud.PACKET_TOOLTIP[rare] still reads 'the only reliable way to a Seed Sunflower'. The catalogue now has two tier-2 plants, so the rare packet rolls between the Sunflower and the Sticky Sundew and the sentence is false. SeedBank.packet_pool already computes the real pool and _refresh_packet_button already swaps the tooltip at runtime, so the surface to fix it exists.
acceptance_criteria: The rare packet's resting tooltip describes what the tier actually contains and stays true as the catalogue grows. A test asserts it does not name a specific plant.

title: STYLE.md and the sprite gate's palette have drifted apart
description: The new tools/svg_style_check.py cross-checks the two places the palette is written down and reports: the gate's PALETTE in test/unit/test_sprite_style.gd carries #5E5E5E (beetle legs/rim) and #D7C9A8 (the seed packet's torn top) which art_src/STYLE.md documents nowhere. So a sprite author reading STYLE.md sees a 30-colour palette while the build enforces 32, and two legitimate colours look like violations until you read the test instead. STYLE.md is described as the measured contract, so it is the document that should be authoritative.
acceptance_criteria: STYLE.md and test_sprite_style.gd's PALETTE list the same colours, and svg_style_check.py's contract advisory is silent.

title: An SVG style-contract linter that does not need the renderer
description: Authoring art_src/sticky_sundew.svg meant reasoning by hand about STYLE.md's palette and geometry rules -- canvas size, centred axis, edge margin, kit-palette-or-blend-of-two -- because the only way to find out whether a sprite drifts is to render it and run test_sprite_style.gd, which needs Godot. A pure-Python check of the SVG's own fills and strokes against STYLE.md would catch a wrong hue or an off-centre axis at authoring time, and would be parallel-safe, which matters because sprite authoring is exactly the kind of task that gets fanned out.
acceptance_criteria: A script reads art_src/*.svg and reports palette and geometry violations without launching Godot, and agrees with test_sprite_style.gd on every sprite currently in the repo.

title: A fifth plant will not fit in the plant bar
description: Hud._plant_bar is a VBoxContainer at y=44 with 56px buttons and 8px separation. Four plants = 248px, ending at y=292, and _packet_button is hard-coded at y=300 -- so the fourth plant fits with exactly 8px to spare and a fifth overlaps the packet buttons. The side panel has no other slack; the selection box already runs to within 16px of the panel foot. The bar needs to scroll, shrink, or become a grid before the catalogue grows again.
acceptance_criteria: A fifth plant can be added without any side-panel control overlapping another. The existing sibling-occlusion test covers the plant bar at full catalogue size.

title: The rare packet is a button that works once per run
description: PlantCatalog holds three plants, tiers 1/1/2, and the rare packet's max_tier is 99 over a single tier-2 plant. So the rare packet is meaningful exactly once per run and then is only a more expensive common packet. The catalogue is the constraint, not the packet system -- a fourth plant is what makes the tier ladder mean anything.
acceptance_criteria: A fourth plant exists with a mechanic none of the current three cover, and the rare packet remains meaningful after the Sunflower is unlocked.

title: The post-mortem can only count what the run lost
description: RunSummary shows five rows and four of them are damage: waves survived, threat reached, beds lost, compost swept, weakest ground. Nothing counts what the player did well, because no counter exists -- Game._on_pest_died is the single kill funnel and increments nothing, no Time. call appears anywhere in game/, and _on_plant_destroyed frees the node without tallying. A post-mortem that can only report losses reads as a scolding rather than a record.
acceptance_criteria: The summary reports at least pests defeated and run duration alongside the losses, with the counters surviving to the end of the run. Unit tests cover each new counter through the real code path that increments it.

title: The Seed Sunflower is the economy plant with nothing on the board to read
description: Sunflower pays YIELD seeds every INTERVAL seconds and calls _bloom() at the payout, but the only readout of when the next payout lands is the click-gated 'Next %d seeds in %.0fs' line in the selection panel. Corn Cobbler now shows its level as a muzzle fan and Chomp Flower shows chew progress as a shrinking ring; the plant whose entire purpose is a clock is the one plant with no clock on the board.
acceptance_criteria: A Sunflower's progress toward its next payout is visible on the board without selecting it, and the payout itself has a moment. Unit test asserts the drawn state tracks seconds_until_next_yield.

title: The HUD still builds a Banner that nothing has called since the post-mortem shipped
description: hud.gd builds a full-width 48px Banner Label on every launch, and show_banner/hide_banner have zero callers anywhere in the repo now that RunSummary replaced the end-of-run banner. It is present in every scene-tree snapshot under .devtools/. The 0.23.0 orphan scan flags hide_banner independently. Either delete it, or give it the job it is obviously shaped for -- a wave-start announcement, which currently goes to the one-line message row and competes with everything else there.
acceptance_criteria: Either the Banner and its two methods are gone and no scene-tree snapshot contains it, or something calls show_banner and a test covers when it appears and when it clears.

title: The HUD is the only part of the game that never moves
description: Zero create_tween calls in hud.gd, while plant.gd, corn_cobbler.gd, chomp_flower.gd, sunflower.gd, pest.gd, title_screen.gd and notebook_screen.gd all animate. The selection box appears instantly, the banner appears instantly, the uproot relabel snaps, and the threat tint jumps between colours rather than easing. GardenTheme.animations_enabled() already exists as the headless gate, so the pattern is established -- the HUD simply never adopted it.
acceptance_criteria: The selection panel, the message row and the threat tint all transition rather than snap, every animation is gated on GardenTheme.animations_enabled(), and the headless suite still passes because each animation layers on an already-correct final state.

title: The common packet button stays lit once its tier is exhausted
description: Hud disables the common packet button only on locked_empty or seeds < cost. Now that a common packet correctly refuses once tier 1 is exhausted, the button stays lit and every click is a refusal message instead of a purchase. SeedBank.packet_pool(tier) already answers this exactly -- the button's disabled condition should include bank.packet_pool(&common).is_empty().
acceptance_criteria: A packet button is disabled when its tier has nothing left to give, and the tooltip says why. Unit test drains tier 1 and asserts the button is disabled.

title: A Corn Cobbler at full bunch looks exactly like a fresh one
description: CornCobbler.LEVELS takes kernels 1 to 2 to 5 and spread_degrees 0 to 14 to 52, and upgrade() only bumps the level integer. Plant loads one texture once and never changes it, and RANGE is flat at every level. So the single most expensive decision in the game -- paying seeds to upgrade -- produces no visible change on the board at all. The only readout is a line in the selection panel, which requires clicking the plant to see.
acceptance_criteria: An upgraded Corn Cobbler is distinguishable from a level-1 one on the board without selecting it. Unit test asserts the visual differs per level.

title: Project-identity devtools verb so a session can prove which build it is driving
description: A sibling git worktree of this project had its own Godot running and answered this session's devtools bus, because user:// is keyed on project name and shared across worktrees. It cost most of one runtime pass: symptoms were 'no Game in the tree' and node-not-found on paths that plainly existed, which reads as your own scene being broken. Register a project verb returning ProjectSettings.globalize_path('res://') plus the git branch, so any session can assert in one call that it is talking to its own build. Upstream fix filed as G-018; this is the local guard.
acceptance_criteria: cmd project_identity returns the absolute res:// path; a documented one-liner in CLAUDE.md compares it against the working directory before a runtime pass.
close_reason: project_identity verb reports project_root, user_dir, git branch/sha read from disk, worktree-aware; verified live against git rev-parse and offline discovery

title: Tint the threat level as it climbs
description: threat_level() renders as a small integer in the same cream as every other readout, so 'this wave is worse than the last' is something the player has to read and compare rather than see. Tint the threat portion of the wave label green -> amber -> red across the level range so the escalation is preattentive. The level is already a pure static function, so this is a colour lookup.
acceptance_criteria: A static Hud.threat_colour(level) with tests pinning the endpoints and monotonic movement between them; the label uses it.
close_reason: Wave readout tints cream->amber->red via static Hud.threat_color(), saturating at level 12; verified live at both ends

title: Placement preview should warn when a non-combat plant is road-adjacent
description: A hungry pest eats whatever plant is nearest and a Sunflower cannot fight back, but nothing on screen says 'this tile is one hungry mutation away from losing your economy plant'. PlacementPreview already computes reach and legality per cell, so this is nearly free now: road-adjacency is one is_path check on the four neighbours, and the preview is the node that would draw the warning. Only applies to plants with PlantCatalog.reach(id) == 0.0 -- a Corn Cobbler next to the road is fine, that is the point of it.
acceptance_criteria: Hovering a grass cell orthogonally adjacent to the road with the Sunflower selected draws a distinct warning cue; the same cell with a Corn Cobbler selected does not; both covered by unit tests.

title: Per-run lane pressure for the end-of-run post-mortem
description: The lane pressure overlay now shows a whole wave's loss distribution, faded by one decay step per wave, which answers 'where did I lose this wave'. It cannot answer 'which cell has bled me all game'. Accumulate a second, never-faded tally alongside the per-wave one and show it on the end-of-run screen, so the post-mortem tells the player where their garden was actually weak.
acceptance_criteria: Board keeps a run-total pressure map separate from the decaying per-wave one; the end-of-run banner or screen renders it; a unit test shows the run map surviving fades that clear the wave map.

title: Show a readable threat level for endless mode
description: Health, speed, count, gap and mutation chance now all climb independently past wave 8 and the player can see none of them -- the HUD just says 'Wave 39 / 8'. Derive one threat number (or a wave-start banner naming what went up this wave) from the five WaveDirector static functions, which are already pure and callable without a running wave. This is a readout, not a new system.
acceptance_criteria: A static WaveDirector.threat_for(wave) that is monotonic past the fixed table and constant inside it, shown on the HUD, with unit tests for both halves.

title: A richer husk should rot faster, so sweep order becomes a decision
description: Husk size and glow now scale with value, but the timer does not: a 9-seed husk and a 2-seed one both rot in exactly CompostMeter.HUSK_LIFETIME (10s). Sweeping in any order is therefore optimal and the board asks nothing. Scale the lifetime inversely with value (a richer husk decays faster) so 'which one first?' is a real decision, and so the new size cue carries urgency as well as worth.
acceptance_criteria: drop_husk stores a per-husk lifetime derived from value; HuskLayer's rot ring reads that instead of the constant; a unit test shows a high-value husk expiring before a low-value one dropped at the same moment.

title: Lane pressure should record every cell pests were lost at, not just the worst
description: Board.record_lane_pressure only ever receives the single furthest-reached cell for a wave (Game._wave_worst_cell), so a wave where pests died at scattered points along the lane only ever lights up the worst one. Recording every cell a pest died/escaped at (not just the max) would draw the whole 'where the damage happened' picture instead of one hot pixel.

title: Endless mode should scale pest health/speed too
description: WaveDirector._endless_groups scales count/gap and mutation_chance_for scales mutation chance as endless mode runs longer, but Pest.SPECIES health/speed stay fixed forever -- a wave-60 pest is exactly as tough as a wave-9 one. Scale health and/or speed slightly past some endless threshold, mirroring the mutation-chance climb, so late-game pressure isn't pure quantity.

title: Husk size/glow should scale with value
description: HuskLayer._draw() draws every husk at a fixed 9px radius regardless of CompostMeter's stored value, so a mutated pest's 1.5-2x husk_multiplier() payout is invisible until clicked. Scale the drawn radius (or ring brightness) by value so a bigger payout reads visually across the board, the way mutation tints already do for the pest itself.

title: Second bite frame for a beetle's long chew
description: chomp_flower_eating.png is one fixed picture for the whole chew animation, aphid or beetle alike, even though a beetle's chew is 2.6s — long enough to read a second frame. Swap in an 'almost done' frame once chew_progress() > 0.6 (the same threshold the shrinking ring already reads) to sell 'big pests take a while' with just a second sprite and one if-check.
close_reason: chomp_flower_eating_late.png swaps in past chew_progress()>0.6 (LATE_BITE_THRESHOLD); verified headless (3 ChompFlower unit tests + sprite style contract) and live (texture path polled across a real slow-motion beetle chew, crossing exactly at 61%)

title: Endless mode should mutate faster over time
description: WaveDirector._endless_groups scales pest count and gap as endless mode continues, but MUTATION_CHANCE stays fixed at 40% forever, so wave 40 looks exactly as 'weird' as wave 8. Scale mutation chance upward (or widen MUTATIONS with a rarer fourth trait) past some endless-mode wave threshold so a long run keeps feeling different.
close_reason: WaveDirector.mutation_chance_for(wave) climbs by 0.02/wave past the fixed table, capped at 0.85; verified headless (4 unit tests) and live (curve sweep matching the exact formula shape)

title: Title screen + endless mode with seed high score
description: Add a title screen and an endless mode variant where waves keep escalating past the fixed 8; track and display a seed-count high score.
close_reason: Implemented and /verify'd in the 2026-08-15 session: sprite pass 2 (eating/dead states), pest mutations from wave 8, tiered seed packets + Seed Sunflower (3rd plant), title screen + endless mode, and the Designer's Notebook screen. See log-devtools.md and kanban.md.

title: Pest mutations from wave 8
description: From wave 8 onward, a random pest type gains one trait: armoured (Chomp chews 2x as long), winged (ignores ground plants), or hungry (eats the plant instead of walking past). Turns the fixed wave table into a different run each time.
close_reason: Implemented and /verify'd in the 2026-08-15 session: sprite pass 2 (eating/dead states), pest mutations from wave 8, tiered seed packets + Seed Sunflower (3rd plant), title screen + endless mode, and the Designer's Notebook screen. See log-devtools.md and kanban.md.

title: Compost meter
description: Pests leave husks on death; sweeping/collecting husks pays out seeds. Rewards active play without adding a second currency to read.
close_reason: Implemented and /verify'd in the 2026-08-15 session: sprite pass 2 (eating/dead states), pest mutations from wave 8, tiered seed packets + Seed Sunflower (3rd plant), title screen + endless mode, and the Designer's Notebook screen. See log-devtools.md and kanban.md.

title: Seed packet tiers
description: Packets are currently a two-item shuffle. Add tiered packets (cheap=common only, expensive=better odds/rarer plant) so buying is a real gamble. Needs a third plant to be meaningful.
close_reason: Implemented and /verify'd in the 2026-08-15 session: sprite pass 2 (eating/dead states), pest mutations from wave 8, tiered seed packets + Seed Sunflower (3rd plant), title screen + endless mode, and the Designer's Notebook screen. See log-devtools.md and kanban.md.

title: Reuse SelectionMarker's pattern for a placement preview cue
description: SelectionMarker (plant-tower-defense-42t) is a sibling Node2D drawn independent of a plant's own _draw() override. The same pattern (corner brackets, dimmer/dashed) could show 'this is where the cursor would place a plant' before the click lands, reusing the exact node/technique instead of inventing a new cursor overlay concept.

title: Designer's Notebook screen
description: A screen showing the original hand-drawn image1.jpg-image6.jpg beside the finished sprite for each plant. The drawings are the source material and should be visible in-game.
close_reason: Implemented and /verify'd in the 2026-08-15 session: sprite pass 2 (eating/dead states), pest mutations from wave 8, tiered seed packets + Seed Sunflower (3rd plant), title screen + endless mode, and the Designer's Notebook screen. See log-devtools.md and kanban.md.
